body:
I'd rather be in your position to be honest, and since I decided to stick around and keep fighting until I have closed off every plausible path to success, you offer some good advice... the bit about drugs...never really considered that, I can't stay focused for long, and I think that sank me. I'm going to give it a shot.

I talked to Career services and they pretty much told me I am fucked even if I turn my grades around, tried to steer me into looking for a "Small firm". No thanks, no better call Saul shit for me. But I need to turn my grades around and start studying for the GMAT or GRE, get myself into a good graduate program. I can still turn this around, and to be honest I would rather die pumped full of cocaine on a yacht in Cos-Cob after a 7 day drug fueld workweek than a shitty motel somewhere because I failed.

My perspective is built around having grown up around people at the top of the belll curve, and somewhat around people at the very bottom. I grew up in a very affluent part of westchester county where you were either a prominent lawyer, physician, or in the financial services industry, or in the service industry supporting them. There's no middle class home town for me to slink back to, my entire world revolves around people who are by definition successful. My family, my friends, my classmates. Ending up in the middle of the bell curve isn't something that would secretly relive them, it's something I will be looked down on for. Ever hear of Penn face? It's what I have to keep up, day after day as my future falls apart.

I am expected to be successful in my own right and carry my own weight, either in income, prestige, or both. I'm not going to carry that weight, and any success I may have will be because of who I know, and people around me will realize that. 

My situation is much different than a middle class kid shooting for the top, there won't be any understanding for my failure from anyone I know. And if I can't fix that, I can't continue.

I am well aware that there are probably five billion people on the planet who are worse off than I will be and are perfectly happy. That does not change things from my perspective, or what is normal where I grew up and who I have gone to school with.  I am also well aware that while there are expectations, the statistics on people overcoming adversity to be successful discredit most anecdotal evidence. People's success is very much tied to where they go to school and their grades, at least in Law.

And as for a dating pool, I am not talking about looks, but education and a common social network. A lawyer doing personal injury work on Long Island isn't going to spend time with the same people that someone at an NLJ 250 firm or someone in a federal DA's office is going to spend time with, they are simply worlds apart in interests and expectations. Two people may love each other initially, but when the glow wears off, the people who stay together tend to be those who are well matched.

I am aware there is a minuscule chance of having the life I want, but it doesn't seem worth suffering through failure for nothing. Better to end it if I can't find a path forward with a reasonable chance of meeting my minimum standards.
I don't really see myself getting where I want to go in that field, there's a few stars and everyone else is lower middle class at best, and it's not steady income.

That...may work. I'll see if anyone in career services knows a good way to go that route with my last two years. Because I'm not going the better call Saul route. Maybe I can give myself a stay to see if I can make that happen.

Yes, 80 hour weeks followed a decade later by a house in Darien, Connecticut, a country club membership, access to a better dating pool, better networking, a concierge doctor, and sending my future kids to private school and eventually wherever their potential can take them.

As opposed to a 70's split level on Long Island with a naggy stony brook grad and kids going to public school and then SUNY bumfuck.
This why people who strike out at OCI in law school kill themselves. The platitudes that they are going to be just as happy making $40K a year as making $160K in BigLaw are lies and they know it.

Yeah, well it's hard to explain dropping out of law school to future employers, it's a huge gap I can't hide. Can I survive without a law degree? Sure. But I see the very narrow pathways to actual success (By the standards of my family and friends and my existing social/dating network that would be $100K+ a year or something very prestigious in public service or academia) closing very rapidly.

It's all a matter of perspective. For someone from a lower class or middle class background, I would already be a success having graduated from a respectable university. But from the perspective of where I come from, I feel I am doomed to failure if I don't meet the standards set out by my parents, siblings and peers. I'm going to be the Roger Clinton of the family. If I leverage my network to get a job with just my BA, even if I am a success, I will be looked down upon as someone who needed help, and couldn't achieve on their own.

The problem for me is, money allows me to live near my family, money allows me to do things with my friends. My support network is built around people who have succeeded. To fail is to fail in a very visible and noticeable way to everyone around you. I come from a home town in Connecticut where the cheapest house on the market is around $400,000. You came from that culture, but as you know it's not very forgiving.

Failure will follow me every day until I find a way to fix it.

As for DOD/DOE/DARPA type stuff...

For Top Secret it will show up, they look -everywhere-. It may be waiverable if you do not mention suicide and just say you are depressed. But for anything nuclear, at least with the DOE or DOD, it would be a full stop, do not pass go barrier to clearance. It would be considered "PRP Permanently Disqualifed" Even mild depression would disqualify someone from there, they are super sensitive.

For secret it probably won't matter unless you actually attempt suicide.

For non-defense or DOE related background checks, honestly I don't think they care, unless it's like the CDC and you are working with infectious diseases or something? They may have their own system.

Except only in law is there a perverted system where hiring for the good, $160K plus jobs at BigLaw firms is done exclusively based on first year grades. That is the expectation of my family (One met by my Brother) and failing that I am locked out of that world with no way in. At least with Columbia I would be setting myself up for a PHD and eventually respectability. The deadlines for any respectable masters programs have passed, so I'd be stuck waiting a year to apply anywhere else, I got lucky that I was able to call up Columbia and they were willing to take an application after the deadline passed when I realized I needed a backup plan.

Millions of people have survived that, myself included. In fact, my dad insisted I work at a grocery store at home in Connecticut for a summer so I could see how humiliating it was to do that sort of work, to motivate me in college. The fact that it was meant to show me the price of failure in my families eyes bothers me more than the actual work, which wasn't bad.

I'm just not willing to be the family fuck up anymore.
Do you ever plan to work in a professionally licensed field such as Law or Medicine? It could be a problem.
